title: Streamlining Claims Processing for Federal Contractor Employees Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Streamlining Claims Processing for Federal Contractor Employees Act - Transfers authority from the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to the Department of Labor for processing claims for wages due to laborers and mechanics hired by contractors on public works projects.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass

summary.headline: A 2013 law moves the job of processing certain wage claims for workers on federal public works projects from the GAO to the Department of Labor.
summary.what_it_does: The law transfers authority to handle claims for unpaid wages owed to laborers and mechanics hired by federal contractors on public works projects. Before this law, the Government Accountability Office handled these claims. After it, the Department of Labor handles them instead. The official summary does not describe any other changes.

who_it_affects.group: Laborers and mechanics employed by federal contractors on public works projects
who_it_affects.how: People who believe they are owed wages on these projects now file wage claims with the Department of Labor instead of the Government Accountability Office.

who_it_affects.group: Federal contractors that perform public works projects
who_it_affects.how: Wage claims from their workers are now processed by the Department of Labor rather than the Government Accountability Office.
The department takes on the work of processing these wage claims.
The agency gives up authority to process these wage claims to the Department of Labor.
